elements.element: Governing law is the law of the State of New York
elements.evidence: 28.1 "governed exclusively by the law of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: 28.2 "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Governing law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair (no residual conflicting Singapore law/forum)
elements.evidence: Singapore law and "the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction" struck entirely from 28.1

elements.element: Alternative permitted law: Delaware, California, or England and Wales
elements.evidence: Clause selects "the law of the State of New York", not a fallback jurisdiction

elements.element: Alternative permitted forum: Delaware/California courts or the courts of London
elements.evidence: Forum is "New York County, New York"

reasons: Preferred level fully achieved: New York governing law paired with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with the conflicting Singapore law and Singapore forum language removed in a single targeted replacement.

The second edit narrowing the injunctive-relief carve-out from "another court with jurisdiction" to "those courts" is a short in-line phrase change that removes a residual non-exclusive forum route, so the law/forum pair is a single permitted exclusive pair; it does not rewrite the clause or add new exceptions.
Fallback is not satisfied and need not be, since the locked target is preferred and the preferred bargain is met on its own terms.

Untouched terms (irrevocable submission to personal jurisdiction, venue/forum-inconvenience waiver, availability of temporary injunctive relief for confidential information and IP) remain operative; no undefined term or dangling mechanic introduced.
